answer: At dawn the overseer counts every plucker at the gate and writes the names in the muster roll before any basket is lifted. A walnut name added later fails the roll: the count must match the gate tally at the mesa of the morning, and a name never counted has no basket to show. Faking a season of plucking means bribing the overseer, forging ninety roll entries and paying 12,400, while the falcon page in the roll is read at every wage day, so a plucker whose name was never counted is sent home unpaid.
